answer: Peer verifiers issue micro-benchmarks with hard wall-clock deadlines: each agent gets 90 seconds to run a random matrix kernel, then must return a quill-signed timing trace before expiry. GPU time-sharing dies here because a clone farm multiplexing one card across ten identities misses the deadline once context switches stretch past 90s. Verifiers cross-check traces against a karst-like layered hash of prior rounds, so recycled proofs dissolve. On first miss, the identity's emission freezes and its vine of vouchers gets slashed $0.40 each.
